top_choice_rationale: P002 rewards a direct prediction-to-experiment chain: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model of magic-angle flat bands was the object that Jarillo-Herrero's group tested in 2018 when it found correlated insulating and superconducting states, and the results are reproduced across many laboratories and extended to other moire systems. A citation limited to the flat-band prediction and the discovery of the states makes no pairing-mechanism claim. The costs are real (about seven years of confirmation, an open mechanism, and Cao and the co-first authors outside the three names), so I rank P001 second. Its two-decade maturity is strong, but Molenkamp tested the BHZ HgTe proposal and not the Kane-Mele model, an attribution break that three names cannot close. P003 has the cleanest credit but I cannot judge Katori's priority or its novelty after the 2005 and 2012 prizes. A prize in one of the three is better than none.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my electronic-structure and magnetism work is field proximity to twisted-bilayer physics, not a connection to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer or any other credited name
